name: trilight
description: Three-channel PWM controller for RGB LEDs. Supports common-cathode (default) and common-anode (is_0_max=True) configurations. Color values 0-255 per channel.

constructor_params.name: is_0_max
constructor_params.description: False: common-cathode (duty=1023 brightest). True: common-anode (duty=0 brightest)

properties.name: color
properties.description: Current (r, g, b) tuple. Each 0-255. Setting auto-applies to PWM.

methods.name: set_rgb
methods.description: Set color via three separate arguments

example:
from machine import Pin
from trilight import TriLight
from time import sleep_ms

light = TriLight(Pin(25), Pin(26), Pin(27))
light.set_rgb(255, 0, 0)   # red
sleep_ms(500)
light.set_color((0, 255, 0))  # green
sleep_ms(500)
light.color = (0, 0, 255)     # blue
light.off()
light.deinit()
esp32_notes: RGB values clamped to 0-255 (out-of-range silently capped)
Common-cathode RGB LED: long leg (anode) to VCC, three short legs via current-limit resistors to GPIO
Common-anode: long leg to GND, three short legs via resistors to GPIO — set is_0_max=True
hardware_notes: Each channel needs 220Ω current-limit resistor (or 100Ω for brighter)
RGB LED draws ~60mA at full white — total GPIO current OK, but consider external driver for higher power
differences_from_standard_mp: Standard code requires three PWM channels + manual mapping. TriLight wraps this with color semantics.
